newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK protesters gear up to greet China Minister Qian.
newsitem.headline: HK protesters gear up to greet China Minister Qian.

text.p: Protesters in Hong Kong prepared to greet Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen by staging a 30-hour hunger strike and sit-in on Thursday outside an exhibition hall he is due to visit.

Brandishing banners and pictures of jailed Chinese dissident Wang Dan, about a dozen pro-democracy activists condemned the formation of Beijing-backed bodies that will take charge of Hong Kong after the territory returns to Chinese rule next year.
Qian, on his first official trip to the colony, will arrive at the Hong Kong Convention Centre on Friday morning to anoint a 400-strong Selection Committee.

Newly-formed under Beijing's tight reins, the body is responsible for selecting Hong Kong's first post-handover Chief Executive and forming a 60-member Provisional Legislature, which will replace the territory's current elected legislature.
"We oppose the Selection Committee, the Provisional Legislature and the way the Chief Executive is chosen," legislator Andrew Cheng and member of Hong Kong's Democratic Party told Reuters.
Cheng, who started his hunger-strike at noon together with eight other protesters, said they would be accompanied throughout the night by some 20 supporters.
Hong Kong, a British colony for a century and a half, will revert to Chinese rule on July 1, 1997.
Although it has been promised a high degree of self-rule for the next 50 years, the colony of 6.3 million people is worried that its freewheeling ways may be curbed.
